source.title: Flip Columns For Maximum Number of Equal Rows

teaching.hint: What property do two rows need to share to become uniform under one common column choice?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Rows that are equal or bitwise complements require the same flip pattern up to an irrelevant flip of every column.
solution_outline.approach: Give each row a signature indicating whether each entry differs from that row’s first entry. Count equal signatures and return the largest count.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The signature records within-row equality relative to column zero and is unchanged by complementing a whole row. Rows with the same signature can be made uniform together.
solution_outline.correctness: For any fixed column-flip set, every uniform resulting row has the same relative pattern; conversely choosing flips at the differing positions makes every row of one signature uniform. Thus the maximum group size is optimal.
solution_outline.complexity: O(mn) expected time and O(mn) space for signatures and counts.
solution_outline.pitfall: Grouping only identical original rows misses rows that are exact complements.

common_wrong_turns: Count only equal rows, not complementary rows
Choose flips separately for each row
source_fidelity_notes: Clarified that one shared column choice is used and that uniform rows need not share the same final bit.
